overall_diagnosis: Plans are being saved in a non–PDDL-compliant text format (function-call style like action(arg1,arg2) or action(args...) as a single token) instead of the canonical parenthesized, whitespace-separated PDDL plan syntax required by unified_planning.io.PDDLReader.parse_plan (e.g., "(action-name arg1 arg2 ...)"). This output-format mismatch causes parse failures before any semantic validation, indicating pddl-skills guidance is underspecified/ambiguous about plan serialization requirements and lacks a recommended re-parse validation step.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill’s plan saving/output requirements are not explicit enough about the exact textual grammar that unified_planning’s PDDLReader.parse_plan (and downstream verifiers) accepts. This likely led to emitting planner/operator strings in function-call syntax (e.g., name(args...)) instead of one-action-per-line s-expressions '(name arg1 ... argN)', causing UPException during plan parsing.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Update SKILL.md to add/strengthen a dedicated 'Plan Saving / Serialization' section that (1) explicitly requires sequential plans to be written one action per line in canonical PDDL plan syntax: '(action-name param1 ... paramN)' with whitespace-separated args inside parentheses; (2) explicitly forbids 'action(param,...)' or 'action(params...)' function-call formatting; (3) notes any casing/normalization expectations (e.g., lowercase) to match parser behavior; (4) optionally documents the temporal/timed line format only if relevant. Include a canonical formatter snippet that converts a unified_planning SequentialPlan into these lines, and require a post-save syntactic check by re-parsing the saved plan with unified_planning.io.PDDLReader.parse_plan before returning/accepting the output.
